newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian officials await decree on Japan PGM talks.
newsitem.headline: Russian officials await decree on Japan PGM talks.

text.p: Russian precious metals officials said on Friday that they were in the dark on when talks with Japan on palladium and platinum supplies would resume, but one source said a decree on the matter should come out this month.
"There are still no developments -- we're still waiting for a government decree," said an unidentified official at the sales department of Almazjuvelirexport, the state precious metals export agency.
"But we have had no word from the government on when this decree will be forthcoming."
A second official echoed the uncertainty but said the matter should be clarified this month.
"It is unknown when the decree will come out, but in theory it should be this month," said Vladimir Rybkin, head of the Finance Ministry's precious metals section.
"But it's hard to say," he said, adding that he could not provide reasons for the delay.
Russia usually holds talks with Japan at the end of each year on supply contracts, but this year the negotiations -- and deliveries -- are already in their fourth month of delay.
Talks were initially held up by delayed passage of the 1997 federal budget and by recent cabinet changes, and are now awaiting a government decree.
Russia is the world's largest palladium producer and Japan is the biggest consumer.
